signals.title: USD/JPY — Geopolitical Risk + Crowded Carry
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.47, holding below its SMA20/50 cluster at 160.49/161.10. Trump’s reiteration of US control over the Strait of Hormuz introduces a geopolitical risk premium into the energy-sensitive pair. While a 275bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage sustains the structural bid, the 25d Risk Reversal at -2.06 indicates extreme hedging demand for JPY strength despite neutral spec positioning. The pair is currently failing to act as a safe haven, with its VIX correlation at +0.399 (z=+1.62σ), suggesting carry-unwind risk is the dominant driver on geopolitical shocks. Trade bias: Neutral/Bearish USD/JPY, intervention and geopolitical risk cap the carry trade. Catalyst: Next BoJ meeting on 18 Sep — hike bias 100% priced. Risk: VIX breaks above 25, reviving the JPY safe-haven function and triggering a disorderly carry unwind.

signals.title: NZD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + RBNZ Hike Bias
signals.text: NZD/JPY displays a dominant G10 bilateral theme as the week's strongest performer (NZD) faces the weakest (JPY). NZD/USD trades at 0.5905, supported by a positive ESI of +7.9 and an active RBNZ hiking cycle at 2.5%. COT data shows NZD spec positioning at a 52-week extreme short (pctl 2, z -2.00), creating an asymmetric short-squeeze setup as price holds above the SMA200 at 0.5835. The 150bp NZD/JPY carry advantage further supports the cross while the G10 spread remains wide at 1.117%. Trade bias: Long NZD/JPY, speculative short-squeeze potential against hawkish RBNZ. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep — hike priced. Risk: RBNZ pauses hiking cycle, validating existing spec shorts.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD at 0.7107 continues to trend higher, positioned firmly above its SMA20/50/200 cluster. Retail sentiment has reached an 85% short extreme, directly fading the institutional trend as COT leveraged funds remain net long +45,727. While the RBA 4.35% vs Fed 3.75% differential provides a 60bp carry tailwind, the negative ESI of -12.7 suggests Australian data is starting to underperform expectations. This divergence between retail fades and institutional adds suggests a potential late-trend squeeze if the retail short continues to grow. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/USD, contrarian to retail extreme. Catalyst: Next RBA meeting 29 Sep — 100% hold priced. Risk: US Dollar reversal on safe-haven flows triggers capitulation of weak institutional longs.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Vol Premium + Carry Divergence
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3545, maintaining a position above the SMA20/50 cluster at 1.3428/1.3374. The options market is pricing a significant 5.0-point Vol Risk Premium, with IV at 11.0% vs HV30 at 6.0%, indicating high demand for protection despite range-bound price action. SONIA 3.73% vs SOFR 3.62% offers a narrow 11bp carry advantage for the Pound, yet COT spec longs remain crowded at a 90th percentile (z +1.23). Fed holds at 3.75%. Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD, high vol premium makes long entry expensive. Catalyst: BoE meeting 17 Sep — hold bias 100% priced. Risk: US data surprises to the upside, reviving Fed hike pricing and forcing a long unwind in GBP.
